newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Overnight rouble rate hits 130 percent - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Overnight rouble rate hits 130 percent - dealers.

text.p: Overnight rouble rates on the Russian interbank money market hit 130 percent during mid-afternoon trading on Tuesday as non-residents selling Treasury Bills returned roubles to the Central Bank and commercial banks sought roubles for Wednesday's T-bill auction, dealers said.
"A hole appeared on the market when non-residents took their money out of GKOs (discount T-bills), bought hard currency and left," said Neftekhimbank dealer Vladimir Zrazhevsky.
Overnight rates were 90-130 percent for smaller banks and 70-90 percent for larger banks after 30-35 percent on Friday.
Zrazhevsky said foreigners sold their GKOs for roubles and then bought Central Bank hard currency with the roubles. "As a result the roubles stayed with the Central Bank," he said.
ABN-Amro dealer Artur Lotov said operators had been selling GKOs since Friday on rumours of a government shake up. Some expect uncertainty to push yields higher at the Wednesday auction.

"Those who had some information about the government changes began to dump GKOs on Friday," Lotov said. "As a result, yields grew sharply and banks are seeking roubles today to throw into the auction tomorrow."
But Konstantin Korishchenko, director of the Central Bank's department for operations on the open market, predicted the trend towards higher GKO yields would not continue on Wednesday.

"I think yields at tomorrow's auction will be lower than the market today. The growth in yields which we say today has a limited nature and there is no serious basis for it and certainly not for panic."
Average GKO yields in secondary trade rose on Tuesday to 32.48 percent from 28.59 percent on Friday, according to the Central Bank.
Korishchenko said that non-residents were likely to continue selling older paper to buy newer issues, which are subject to a profits tax that affects domestic buyers but not most foreigners.
